articles.title: 'Vamos buscar a autossuficiência em diesel', diz Magda sobre plano da Petrobras até 2031 | G1
articles.standfirst: Petrobras prevê investir US$ 122 bilhões até 2031 e ampliar a produção de combustíveis no país. Plano inclui retomada do etanol, parceria com empresa do agronegócio e redução do endividamento da estatal.
articles.summary: Petrobras prevê investir US$ 122 bilhões até 2031 e ampliar a produção de combustíveis no país. Plano inclui retomada do etanol.
articles.body:
Magda Chambriard toma posse como presidente da Petrobras — Foto: André Ribeiro/Agência Petrobras

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Petrobras pretende alcançar a autossuficiência em diesel até 2031 , com capacidade para atender 100% da demanda brasileira pelo combustível. A meta foi anunciada nesta terça-feira (24) pela presidente da estatal, Magda Chambriard, durante a apresentação do plano de negócios da companhia para os próximos cinco anos.

Segundo Magda, a estratégia é ampliar a oferta de derivados produzidos no país e reduzir a necessidade de recorrer a combustíveis importados para abastecer o mercado interno.

"Vamos buscar, ao longo desses próximos cinco anos, a autossuficiência em diesel. O que quero dizer com isso é fazer com que a Petrobras entregue ao mercado brasileiro, em cinco anos, diesel de forma a atender 100% da nossa demanda", afirmou.

A presidente também estima que a Petrobras recolha R$ 1,6 trilhão em tributos nos próximos cinco anos. Segundo ela, a estatal pagou mais de R$ 1 trilhão em impostos e contribuições no período dos últimos cinco anos. Somente no ano passado, foram R$ 277 bilhões. Neste ano, o valor já ultrapassou R$ 250 bilhões.

Para alcançar os objetivos, a companhia aprovou um plano de negócios para 2027 a 2031, com previsão de investimentos de US$ 122 bilhões (cerca de R$ 723 bilhões). O montante representa um aumento de 11,9% em relação aos US$ 109 bilhões previstos para o período de 2026 a 2030. A maior parte dos recursos, US$ 86 bilhões (R$ 509 bilhões), será destinada à exploração e produção de petróleo e gás.

Petrobras não prevê aumentar dívida e promete reduzir endividamento

A presidente da Petrobras afirmou que o plano de negócios 2027-2031 não prevê aumento da dívida da companhia . Segundo ela, os investimentos serão financiados com a geração de caixa da própria estatal, e a estratégia é reduzir o endividamento ao longo dos próximos cinco anos.

"A prioridade do nosso plano é crescer, gerando valor. Portanto, tudo isso tem que ser sustentável e financiável com geração de caixa da companhia. Nós não estamos falando em aumentar dívida nesse plano. Nós estamos falando em reduzir dívida", declarou.

Magda também explicou a composição do endividamento da Petrobras.

Segundo ela, uma parcela corresponde à dívida financeira propriamente dita, que classificou como pequena em relação à capacidade de geração de caixa da empresa.

Outra parte está relacionada à contratação de sondas, plataformas, barcos de apoio e aeronaves utilizados nas operações.

Esses contratos de afretamento — modalidade de contratação para utilização de embarcações e equipamentos — são registrados como dívida no balanço da companhia, embora estejam diretamente ligados à atividade produtiva.

"Eu não chamo isso de dívida. Eu chamo isso de custo operacional, mas no nosso balanço isso é registrado como dívida", afirmou.

A presidente argumentou que a necessidade de contratar mais equipamentos e embarcações acompanha o crescimento da produção de petróleo e gás.

"Produção maior, mais necessidade de afretamentos, mais necessidade de endividamento. Portanto, é a dívida boa", disse.

Ao defender a capacidade da companhia de executar o plano, Magda afirmou que os projetos serão submetidos a critérios rigorosos de retorno financeiro , inclusive em cenários econômicos desfavoráveis.

"Isso significa que nós temos hoje um mantra na Petrobras: rigor em cada decisão e absoluta disciplina de capital", declarou.

Segundo ela, os investimentos precisam apresentar retorno positivo mesmo em condições desafiadoras. A presidente resumiu a estratégia como um plano ambicioso, mas condicionado à preservação do equilíbrio financeiro da estatal.

Petrobras mantém previsão de produzir 2,9 milhões de barris de petróleo por dia até 2031

A Petrobras prevê manter a produção de petróleo em 2,9 milhões de barris por dia ao longo dos próximos cinco anos , segundo a presidente da companhia. Ela afirmou que a estatal poderá superar esse patamar caso novos ativos entrem em operação, mas ressaltou que essa possibilidade não representa um compromisso da empresa.

“Provavelmente nós vamos superar essa marca de 2,9 [milhões de barris por dia]. Por que estou dizendo isso? Provavelmente porque isso não é uma promessa, é só uma especulação. Se tivermos possibilidade, faremos, se for financiável, se for econômico, se for feito com disciplina de capital, se for resiliente a preços baixos. Faremos”, afirmou.

Para alcançar esse patamar, a companhia planeja instalar nove novos sistemas de produção e executar dezenas de projetos complementares de desenvolvimento entre 2027 e 2031 , segundo a presidente Magda Chambriard.

A estatal também pretende ampliar a capacidade de produção de plataformas que já estão em operação e de outras que foram contratadas. Magda destacou que a Petrobras já conseguiu acrescentar 282 mil barris por dia à capacidade de 11 plataformas.

Agora, a intenção é ampliar esse ganho para 520 mil barris diários, considerando também as plataformas da série P-80, P-81, P-82, P-83, P-84 e P-85.

Segundo a presidente, o aumento de capacidade poderá evitar a necessidade de construir novas plataformas para produzir esse volume adicional. Ela estimou que a construção de unidades com capacidade para produzir 520 mil barris por dia exigiria investimentos de US$ 10 bilhões a US$ 12 bilhões.

"O que nós estamos dizendo é que esse dinheiro não será necessário porque haverá expansão de capacidades nas plataformas existentes e nas plataformas já contratadas", afirmou Magda.

A gestão dos reservatórios do pré-sal também será importante para alcançar os resultados previstos, com o aproveitamento do potencial dos campos e a melhoria do desempenho das unidades de produção existentes.

Pré-sal responde por quase 90% da produção brasileira de petróleo, diz Magda

A presidente da Petrobras afirmou que o pré-sal já responde por quase 90% da produção de petróleo do Brasil e destacou a produtividade dos campos da região como um dos pilares do plano de negócios da companhia para 2027 a 2031.

Segundo ela, os ativos do pré-sal são referências mundiais em eficiência e tecnologia, com destaque para o campo de Búzios , que classificou como o maior do mundo em águas profundas e ultraprofundas.

A executiva lembrou que, há cerca de 15 anos, havia dúvidas sobre a viabilidade econômica e operacional do pré-sal, que era considerado caro e difícil de desenvolver. Hoje, afirmou, a região se tornou um ativo de referência internacional e sua produção está incorporada às projeções do novo plano.

Ao falar sobre a estratégia de exploração da companhia, Magda comparou o desenvolvimento do pré-sal ao potencial da Margem Equatorial . Segundo ela, a Petrobras pretende repetir na nova fronteira exploratória o processo de pesquisa, avaliação e desenvolvimento que permitiu ampliar a produção no pré-sal.

A presidente afirmou que a estatal concluiu uma etapa de perfuração na Margem Equatorial e que a sonda foi deslocada para o poço Mãe de Ouro, no Rio Grande do Norte.

A companhia fez três descobertas na região e, no primeiro trimestre de 2027, pretende retomar a perfuração no bloco FZA-M-59, no Amapá. Magda disse que há outros três poços previstos para avaliar o tamanho das jazidas e definir como a área poderá ser desenvolvida.

Ela também citou a continuidade da exploração na Bacia de Pelotas, o desenvolvimento dos campos do pré-sal e a manutenção da produção na Bacia de Campos como parte do planejamento para os próximos anos.

Magda afirmou ainda que a expansão da produção precisa vir acompanhada de investimentos no refino, para que a Petrobras agregue valor ao petróleo no próprio país, em vez de exportar o produto bruto. Segundo ela, a ampliação do parque de refino é estratégica para aumentar o retorno da companhia, especialmente diante das tensões geopolíticas internacionais.

Petrobras terá 42% da Neomille, que poderá elevar produção de etanol a 1,5 bilhão de litros por ano

A Petrobras aprovou um investimento de R$ 2,9 bilhões para adquirir 42% de participação na Neomille, empresa do grupo Cerradinho Bio. O acordo marca a retomada da atuação da estatal na produção de etanol.

Durante a abertura da coletiva, Magda destacou a operação como um passo importante para a volta da Petrobras ao setor. Segundo ela, a companhia estava devendo esse retorno havia pelo menos dois anos.

"É uma satisfação imensa assinar essa entrada da Petrobras na produção de etanol de milho e na utilização do etanol de milho para a nossa produção de combustíveis, cada vez mais sustentáveis e cada vez mais modernos", afirmou.

A Cerradinho Bio continuará no controle da Neomille, enquanto a Petrobras terá participação de 42% na empresa. A estatal também indicará dois diretores, responsáveis pelas áreas de logística e administração e novos negócios, e participará dos comitês de gestão.

Atualmente, a Neomille possui duas usinas, localizadas em Chapadão do Céu (GO) e Maracaju (MS), que produzem cerca de 800 milhões de litros de etanol por ano. Segundo Magda, a capacidade poderá chegar a 1,5 bilhão de litros anuais no curto prazo. A expansão acompanha o plano da empresa de aumentar a produção em 80% nos próximos dois anos..

Magda Chambriard, da Petrobras, faz acordo com Neomille S.A. — Foto: Isabela Ortiz/g1

Pelo acordo, a Petrobras poderá adquirir até 42% do etanol produzido pela Cerradinho e até 90% do óleo técnico de milho fabricado pela Neomille. Os produtos poderão ser utilizados na fabricação de diferentes combustíveis.

O óleo de milho poderá ser aproveitado na produção de diesel coprocessado nas refinarias da Petrobras no Sudeste. O coprocessamento consiste na utilização conjunta de matérias-primas de origem fóssil e vegetal na fabricação de combustíveis.

O insumo também poderá ser utilizado na produção de biodiesel e de combustível sustentável de aviação (SAF, na sigla em inglês). Já o etanol poderá servir como matéria-prima para a fabricação de SAF por diferentes rotas tecnológicas.

Segundo Magda, a parceria também permitirá antecipar em dois anos as exigências do Corsia no Brasil. O mecanismo internacional estabelece regras para a redução e compensação das emissões de gases de efeito estufa em voos internacionais.

A presidente afirmou que a transição energética exigirá diferentes fontes de energia e que a parceria busca conciliar sustentabilidade e segurança energética, em um cenário internacional marcado por conflitos e pela preocupação com as mudanças climáticas.

"Eu gosto de dizer o seguinte: eu olho para o Bernardo e digo assim: Bernardo, não me apareça aqui só com um projeto de etanol. Me apareça com um projeto que faça sentido nesse escopo todo com que estamos lidando", declarou, em referência à parceria.

Acordo prevê integração logística e fornecimento de combustíveis

A parceria também prevê o fornecimento preferencial, pela Petrobras, de até 50% da demanda da Cerradinho Bio e da Neomille por diesel, ureia e enxofre, mediante negociação direta entre as empresas.

Segundo Magda, o acordo estabelece uma relação comercial de mão dupla: enquanto a estatal poderá comprar parte da produção de etanol e óleo de milho da parceira, também poderá fornecer combustíveis e outros produtos ao grupo.

"É um ganha-ganha, é um negócio de mão dupla. Ela tem que valer nos dois sentidos. Quando só um ganha, a relação se rompe", afirmou a presidente.

A Petrobras também adquiriu a totalidade da participação na Logum, empresa responsável por uma infraestrutura de transporte de etanol por dutos. Segundo Magda, a estrutura poderá ser integrada à produção da Neomille a partir de 2028, com a expansão da capacidade das usinas.

A intenção é conectar a produção do Centro-Oeste às principais rotas comerciais de etanol do Sudeste, ampliando as possibilidades de transporte e distribuição do biocombustível.

A companhia também pretende estreitar a relação com o agronegócio, especialmente nas regiões Centro-Oeste e Matopiba, que abrange áreas do Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia.

Entre as possibilidades mencionadas por Magda estão o fornecimento de diesel a produtores e empresas do agronegócio e o aproveitamento do dióxido de carbono (CO₂) de origem biogênica — gerado a partir de fontes renováveis — em rotas de produção de combustíveis de baixo carbono.

"Temos também a aproximação com o agronegócio como um foco, tanto como cliente de diesel quanto pelo aproveitamento do CO₂ biogênico em rotas de produção de combustíveis de baixo carbono. O Centro-Oeste nos interessa, e a Cerradinho faz parte disso. O Matopiba também nos interessa muito e, provavelmente, a Cerradinho fará parte dessa estratégia", afirmou.

Magda classificou a parceria como uma oportunidade de crescimento para as duas empresas. Ela também reconheceu as diferenças entre as estruturas das companhias, já que a Petrobras precisa seguir processos burocráticos e prestar contas aos órgãos de controle.

"A Petrobras é mestre em entregas. Quando a gente se dispõe, a gente entrega", afirmou.

articles.title: Don’t Panic, Buy These Instead: Jim Cramer’s Emergency 5-Stock Portfolio
articles.summary: By November 18, the S&P 500 had fallen for five straight sessions, its longest losing streak since June. Yet the index was still up 7% for the year, accordin...
articles.body:
By November 18, the S&P 500 had fallen for five straight sessions, its longest losing streak since June. Yet the index was still up 7% for the year, according to the Associated Press. Investors looking at their own accounts had reason to wonder how both things could be true. On the previous evening's Mad Money , CNBC's Jim Cramer counted 184 stocks in the S&P 500 that had fallen at least 20% from their 52-week highs. More than a third of the index had already suffered a decline of that size.

The pressure had been building since October, when the Nasdaq 100 lost 6.6%, its steepest monthly decline in 18 months. Reuters reported that rising borrowing costs for AI projects and doubts about what those investments would earn had weighed on the market. The selling could feed on itself. Hedge fund research firm PivotalPath found growing overlap in the U.S. stock holdings of ten large multistrategy managers. It noted that if several cut risk at once, selling could concentrate in the same stocks.

Cramer heard from callers who took a falling share price as a verdict on the business they owned. He saw selling move from software and hardware into banks, transportation and housing. He was hesitant to commit more money to tech without a change in the way buyers responded to early losses . Even so, he was willing to buy individual stocks where he thought the price already reflected the bad news.

So, what is the don't panic, buy these instead: Jim Cramer's emergency 10-stock portfolio? We provided the expanded list of Don't Panic, Buy These Instead: Jim Cramer's Emergency 10-Stock Portfolio here. The top 5 stocks are provided below.

We reviewed stocks Cramer discussed publicly in October and November and selected 5 for which he recommended buying after a decline, named a lower price or price condition at which he would consider buying, or favored starting a position during the November turbulence. Where several stocks qualified, we gave preference to calls that identified the decline or explained how to build the position. The list was compiled from separate public calls, including ones made on Mad Money, all of which fell in November. We ranked the stocks in ascending order of market capitalization.

Don't Panic, Buy These Instead: Jim Cramer's Emergency 5-Stock Portfolio

5. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS )

Cramer's Charitable Trust put money behind its The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) call. During the November 5 selloff, it announced plans to buy 10 shares at roughly $867 each. The following day's portfolio review confirmed it had added to the position . Cramer had already taken a close look at the shares after an earlier decline. His October answer to a Goldman question helps explain why the Trust had an appetite for another purchase when markets turned .

articles.title: Govt pushes livelihood creation, productive use of exhausted mines in new closure rules
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt has made the conversion of exhausted mines into productive assets -- including solar power sites, eco-parks, agricultural land and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt has made the conversion of exhausted mines into productive assets -- including solar power sites, eco-parks, agricultural land and fisheries -- a key part of its revised mine closure framework, while making companies more accountable for creating alternative livelihoods for communities dependent on mining.The new guidelines, which build on the framework introduced in 2025, make it mandatory for coal and lignite companies to provide mechanised systems for loading coal and adopt blast-free mining as the norm, while allowing drilling and blasting only where such technology is technically unfeasible or commercially unviable. Mines with a capacity of 2 million tonnes per annum or more will also have to plan for transporting coal through modes other than road, as far as practicable, within five years of starting production.The guidelines have assigned a greater role to district administrations and local communities in deciding what happens after a mine is closed, making establishment of a committee mandatory in every district with mining operations to oversee livelihood projects, skill training and the involvement of local communities and self-help groups in activities such as maintenance of public spaces and other facilities.“Companies will also have to assess the impact of mine closure on people living in and around the mining area, including a buffer zone of around 10 km, to identify opportunities for alternative livelihoods,” said an official. The rules have also changed how companies must spend money set aside for mine closure.The changes come as govt steps up efforts to scientifically close and repurpose exhausted coal mines. The coal ministry has set up a dedicated corpus of around Rs 40,000 crore for scientific and progressive mine closure, environmental restoration and repurposing of exhausted mines. India scientifically closed 42 coal mines, including 33 blocks, in the preceding year, while govt has identified 147 mines for scientific closure over the next 2-3 years.Coal ministry said the guidelines will come into force 30 days from the date of their issuance and will provide an outcome-oriented framework for systematic and scientific mine planning and mine closure. “Keeping pace with emerging technologies, the guidelines recognise underground coal gasification as a mining method. These are expected to improve ease of doing business through simpler, practical and time-bound processes, and to accelerate the operationalisation of mines, supporting the country’s energy security,” the ministry said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: A low-Huanging fruit? Jensen burner may have netted Trump a $15 million windfall
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump has never been shy about claiming credit for a good deal.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump has never been shy about claiming credit for a good deal. His latest presidential intervention, however, may have delivered a whopping personal windfall: by some estimates as much as $15 million in gains on his Nvidia stock after he persuaded the company to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.Nvidia shares surged 31.5 per cent on Monday, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value after its board reversed Huang's departure, barely 11 days after he resigned following an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese spy agencies. An analysis of Trump's latest financial disclosures by the Financial Times estimated that his Nvidia holdings could have appreciated by between $1.3 million and $15 million in Monday's rally alone.The wide range reflects the imprecise nature of the disclosures, which report transactions in dollar bands rather than exact share counts. Depending on the assumptions about purchases and sales, Trump may have held anywhere between 32,000 and 370,000 shares as of September 30. His latest disclosure, filed on November 5, records several Nvidia purchases in September, including transactions in a range reaching $250,000. Crucially, it does not cover October or November, leaving unanswered the question of whether he bought or sold shares during the period immediately preceding Huang's reinstatement.The $15 million, therefore, is a potential paper gain, not a realised profit. Nor does it establish that Trump traded on inside information. But the coincidence is remarkable enough to invite questions about the intersection of presidential influence and personal financial interests, an issue Democrats -- some of whom are also accused of being on the make -- are ready to get their teeth into.Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday. "And I convinced them ... I made the deal." The MAGA boss was not merely cheering from the sidelines either. According to reports, veep JD Vance, himself a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist, also intervened over the weekend, acting as an emissary to Nvidia's boardThe board eventually capitulated, saying it had received assurances from senior US government officials that Huang's return did not pose a national security risk. Trump himself virtually absolved Alice Huang of being an intelligence operative despite leaks from the US intel about her ties to Chinese agencies, saying any beautiful woman who comes from China is usually dubbed a spy.The White House's defence about alleged Trump profiteering is that his portfolio is managed by independent third-party financial institutions, which make investment decisions without his involvement and replicate broad market indices such as the Schwab 1000. The administration has also described his assets as being held in a trust managed by his children, although the precise management arrangements have not always been explained consistently.Experts say all this does not eliminate the underlying conflict: a president can influence the fortunes of companies in which his family-controlled financial arrangements have significant exposure. Besides, Nvidia is hardly an isolated case, although the President's broader financial portfolio makes the Nvidia episode particularly striking. Trump's latest annual disclosure, covering 2025, showed that he received more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures, including World Liberty Financial, the family-backed crypto business liked to Pakistan, and his $TRUMP meme coin. The proceeds have helped swell his conventional stock and bond portfolio to an estimated $703 million to $2.6 billion by the end of last year, according to a Reuters analysis.The growing perception among critics is that the Trump family and its business associates are making off like bandits while the President presides over decisions that can move markets and determine corporate fortunes. The concern is not necessarily that every transaction is improper, but that the administration has blurred the boundary between public authority and private enrichment to an extent rarely seen in modern American politics.The Nvidia affair is particularly striking because it follows Trump's extraordinary intervention at Intel last year. After publicly questioning the national security credentials of Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and demanding his removal over his past China connections, Trump changed course following a White House meeting. The eventual arrangement gave the US government a 10 per cent non-voting stake in the struggling chipmaker, converting $11.1 billion in government grants and commitments into shares.Trump himself described the deal as something he had personally negotiated. The government became one of Intel's largest shareholders, while Tan retained his job. Nvidia now presents an even more unusual variation of the same phenomenon. Washington does not own a stake in the company, as it does in Intel. But its influence over Nvidia's leadership, export permissions and national security standing has become unmistakable. The company has effectively discovered that its boardroom decisions can require presidential blessing.The Wall Street Journal, among others, has described Nvidia as having become, in effect, a government-backed enterprise. Huang owes his reinstatement to Trump, and the company's ability to navigate its continuing legal and regulatory troubles may depend considerably on the administration's goodwill.Meanwhile, Congress, which is itself far from being a paragon of virtue, is up in arms. Raja Krishnamoorthi, the Illinois Democrat who chairs the House Select Committee on China, called Huang's reinstatement "outrageous," arguing that neither the government nor Nvidia's board had completed its investigation into what information Chinese intelligence might have obtained. He has demanded a full public congressional hearing, insisting that the American people deserve answers.Even Republicans are asking uncomfortable questions. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, always ready with colorful observations, said it was not his business to police Huang's marital conduct while calling it “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” But a relationship with someone potentially connected to Chinese intelligence was an entirely different matter because it jeopardizes national security, he said, adding that he wanted officials to explain whether export controls had been circumvented. He also called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to answer questions under oath about the handling of the suspected chip-diversion affair.The controversy is gradually feeding into a wider Washington debate about the extraordinary monetisation of political access, a debate complicated by the fact that lawmakers from both sides have been accused of minting money with insider info. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi has faced years of scrutiny over the spectacular investment returns associated with trades made by her husband, venture capitalist Paul Pelosi.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: CEO of $21 billion Cerebras says it’s minted 1,000 employees into millionaires—but warns that drastic changes in fortunes can be ‘really stressful’
articles.summary: Billionaire Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said: “Change is stressful, and the vast changes in your personal wealth both up and down are really stressful.”
articles.body:
Employees at some of the largest tech companies are scoring big thanks to stock purchase benefits . Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman says he's proud that his $21.7 billion AI company has turned over a thousand of its staffers into millionaires. But he knows firsthand how quickly those fortunes can change—and says employees shouldn't get too caught up in watching their net worth yo-yo.

"What we've done with our team first, we made more than a thousand millionaires," Feldman recently said on the Sourcery With Molly O'Shea channel. "That's something I'm really proud of. I think that's our job as leaders, to make our guys wealthy. We talked about the fact that we're not in this for the short run, that the daily fluctuations are not what they should watch."

As tech companies rule the U.S. stock market, all it takes is a bad earnings report or a shift in investor sentiment to send company shares on a roller-coaster ride.

Now founders and employees alike can watch their fortunes fluctuate in the span of one day. Eligible employees at Cerebras can buy company stock directly through deductions from their paychecks at a potential 15% discount, according to the company's 2026 employee stock purchase plan (ESPP). In May, Cerebras had a standout IPO offering 30 million Class A shares at price of $185 per share, raising $5.55 billion.

Feldman's share was estimated to be worth about $3.2 billion following the IPO, but the CEO warned workers against watching their wealth swing at the whim of the stock market.

"Change is stressful. And the vast changes in your personal wealth, both up and down, are really stressful. It's further made challenging by the fact that your wealth is fluctuating every day—and sometimes intraday," Feldman continued. "You try and teach people that these fluctuations that we have no control of, can't be watched."

Fortune reached out to Cerebras for comment.

The CEO's wealth once changed more than his father's entire lifetime earnings

Feldman understands how wealth can change on a dime all too well.

As the cofounder of both Cerebras and SeaMicro with previous stints at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Force10 Networks, and Riverstone Networks, he's seen how stock prices fluctuate in scaling tech companies.

The CEO recalled that while working for a different business, the stock would swing up and down, impacting his equity. Within one day, his personal wealth changed more than his father had made in his entire lifetime, Feldman said.

"For a while my dad called me every day and said, 'Why is your stock down?' Like, 'Dad, that's not helpful. Come on, Dad. I know it's down, but I don't know why,'" Feldman continued during the podcast. "You have to modulate when it's up—your psyche—and you've got to modulate when it's down. And you've got to think about what your job is every day."

articles.title: Microsoft declares a code red in the middle of a 'Patchpocalypse'
articles.summary: After a 24-hour outage, Microsoft is racing to speed up fixes that took nearly a week to reach customers.
articles.body:
Companies are racing to patch a record number of software flaws this year. Microsoft just found out how long its own fixes take to reach the world.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) has declared a code red, its top-priority alarm, after a 24-hour outage this month, according to internal memos reported by Reuters . The goal is to fix future problems worldwide within an hour. A recent urgent fix took five to six days to reach everyone.

The Nov. 12-13 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams, and Copilot . The culprit was a flaw in Microsoft's own software , introduced in July, that went unnoticed for about four months. Microsoft ruled out hackers and AI agents .

Microsoft promises business customers that Microsoft 365 will be up 99.9% of the time, which allows about 44 minutes of downtime a month. By Yahoo Finance calculations, one 24-hour outage used up nearly three years' worth, though not every customer was down that long.

Responders traded more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats while the data they needed sat scattered across separate systems. The faulty component had "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures," Charles Lamanna, a Microsoft executive vice president, said in a code red review.

The fix list includes dividing traffic by region, so trouble in one place doesn't spread everywhere, and also AI agents that comb through system data to find problems faster.

It all comes in the middle of what Ben Emons of FedWatch Advisors calls a " Patchpocalypse ," a flood of newly discovered software flaws, many found by AI, that companies have to fix. Newly reported flaws hit a record of almost 17,500 in October. Emons warned that "every patch is a chance for something to break."

Speed is now everyone's problem. Cisco ( CSCO ) President Jeetu Patel told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that the time between a flaw going public and an attack "is actually shrinking now, to minutes."

The numbers back him up. In 2018-19, attackers took an average of 63 days to exploit a newly revealed flaw, according to Google's Mandiant. In 2024, attacks began on average a day before a fix was even available. Mandiant estimates that head start grew to about a week in 2025.

"You can't just wait on these patches ... because patches are complicated. You have to bring down the system," Patel said. Cisco and OpenAI released a free tool Monday that puts temporary "shields" on systems while a fix is tested.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on the same show that OpenAI once put a quarter of its production engineers on security alone, and every company should do the same.

articles.title: Kohl's stock soars after retailer posts sales growth for first time in 4 years
articles.summary: Kohl's just snapped an 18-quarter sales slump.
articles.body:
For the first time in four years, Kohl's ( KSS ) has posted positive comparable sales growth. The stock was up 15% by midday Tuesday after the company showcased its turnaround in its third quarter earnings report and raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook.

Here's what Kohl's reported in Q3, versus analyst estimates:

Comparable sales increased 1.2%, compared to Wall Street estimates of a 0.5% decline.

Revenue of $3.45 billion was up 1.3% from a year earlier, above analyst estimates of $3.39 billion.

Earnings per share were $1.76, compared to estimates of break-even earnings.

Kohl's reported a profit of $254 million, but the quarter had help. The results included a $137 million tax benefit from settled tax examinations, a $61 million gain on the sale of two properties, and about $45 million in tariff refunds. Even so, the numbers point to a major turnaround for a retailer that earned only $8 million in Q3 last year.

Kohl's had gone more than four years without topline growth. As of the second quarter, comparable sales had fallen for 18 consecutive quarters as the retailer struggled with inflation pressures and online competitors.

Interestingly, the gains weren't from Kohl's partnership with makeup retailer Sephora. Sephora shop-in-shops fell nearly 2%, executives told analysts Tuesday, but Kohl's CEO Michael Bender said he still supported the partnership.

"We feel good about the progress that we're making with Sephora," Bender, who permanently stepped into his role in the department store roughly a year ago, said on Tuesday.

Kohl's expects the momentum to carry into the fourth quarter, forecasting comparable sales growth of up to 2%. Analysts had anticipated 0.2%. For the full year, the company now expects sales to be flat to up 0.5%, compared with prior guidance of flat to down 1.5%.

Other big box stores, including Target ( TGT ), Walmart ( WMT ), and TJX ( TJX ), also posted better-than-expected results and increased traffic this earnings season.

Kohl's stock is up more than 19% since January.

articles.title: Why Trump wanted Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia
articles.summary: President Trump and Vice President Vance view Huang as a vital defender of open-source AI models.
articles.body:
At the center of the White House's push to get Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO of Nvidia was a conviction that he plays a critical role in keeping the artificial intelligence sector competitive.

According to a source familiar with the matter, President Trump and Vice President Vance view Huang as a vital defender of open-source AI models — which offer users greater control, customization, privacy, and cost flexibility — and believe his leadership is necessary to prevent closed-source AI developers from consolidating power.

Trump and Vance worked through the weekend to bring Huang back. After behind-the-scenes persuasion from the White House, Nvidia's board staged a stunning reversal Monday, returning Huang to the CEO position.

Prior to the reinstatement, the president and vice president were briefed on the national security dimensions of the situation. Both concluded there was no evidence Huang had engaged in any illegal or improper conduct regarding US national security. According to the source, Trump believes maintaining a close working relationship with Huang offers the administration the strongest opportunity to safeguard national security and prevent advanced chips from reaching prohibited buyers.

Trump said during a CNBC interview Monday that Nvidia's board had sought assurances that Huang did not pose a national security threat due to his ties to Alice Huang, a Singapore-based Megaspeed executive suspected of links to Chinese intelligence with whom he had an affair.

Huang resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging that and other extramarital affairs, but was reinstated after just 12 days.

In a post on Truth Social on Monday, Trump urged the company to maintain strict oversight, writing, "NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."

Trump also noted that his assessment aligned with the Justice Department's. A Justice Department official confirmed that Attorney General Todd Blanche spoke with the president over the weekend, and that the department has found no evidence of wrongdoing by either Huang or Nvidia.

Addressing reporters at a press conference Tuesday, Blanche said, "To the extent that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that's something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true," when asked whether Huang had been investigated.

articles.title: Michigan AD deal with Trev Alberts 'pathetic,' says one labor lawyer
articles.summary: Two labor lawyers say the University of Michigan appears to be on the hook for its deal with Trev Alberts, who will never work at the school.
articles.body:
The University of Michigan appears to be on the hook for its deal for an athletic director who will never work at the school.

So said two labor lawyers who have successfully sued U-M in the past.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Michigan agreed with then-Texas A&M Trev Alberts in a memorandum of understanding that it would hire him to be athletic director, paying him more than $17 million over five years. Within a week, the school scuttled the deal amid allegations that Alberts botched a sexual misconduct allegation at his former employer, the University of Nebraska.

"As a result of the information gathered as part of the employment process, the university had determined the background check is not acceptable to the university," current U-M President Domenico Grasso and President-elect C. Cybele Raver wrote to Alberts in a letter dated Nov. 24 .

Alberts' agent, Tom Mars, responded that his client is owed the full amount spelled out in the MOU.

Deborah Gordon, an employment law specialist in Bloomfield Hills, who reviewed the letter and the MOU for the Free Press, called the school's letter "pathetic."

"It's a bunch of B.S.," she said. "That should have been done before you put the document in front of the guy to sign. You signed a memorandum of understanding that's binding and you didn't even do a background check? Are you flipping kidding me?"

Gordon won a whistleblower protection lawsuit in 2022 that was filed against U-M by a police officer at the school's Dearborn campus who said the school mishandled a sexual assault allegation by a female student against a professor.

She said U-M could have easily included a line in the MOU making the offer subject to the successful completion of a background check. But the MOU as written doesn't include that language.

It does include language saying that the formal agreement between the parties "will contain additional customary terms and conditions consistent with executive employment agreements of this nature."

In the Nov. 24 letter, U-M said: "Among the customary terms and conditions of the employment process at the University of Michigan is the successful completion of a background check."

"Like, we have to come up with something, let's say we didn't finish our background check ," Gordon said. "People, that is on you, nor does your memorandum of understanding say this is contingent upon completion of a background check."

Sarah Prescott is a Northville lawyer who represented eight women who sued U-M claiming they were sexually harassed by Martin Philbert, the former provost and chief academic officer. Prescott negotiated a $9 million settlement with the school in 2020.

She reviewed the letter and the memo as well. Prescott said the school's argument that it was going to include the background check condition in the final agreement is weak, but a second point in the school's letter is a little stronger.

The section of the letter reads: "The information gathered in the background check provides good cause to terminate the MOU between the parties."

"The second argument is we could terminate you for cause," Prescott said. "And it says so right in this very same document that you say is binding on both of us."

The MOU doesn't define "for cause," but there are examples from other sources, Prescott said.

"It doesn't mean that it's just nothing, like you can fire them for anything," she said. "But it doesn't mean that you have to have a crime committed and so it becomes what's essentially, quote unquote, good cause ."

The letter doesn't identify what that information in the background check was that sunk the deal, but the timing suggests reports on his work at his alma mater, the University of Nebraska, may have prompted it.

Alberts, 56, is accused in a Title IX lawsuit of ignoring a basketball player's claim that one of her Nebraska coaches groomed her for sex.

In a suit filed in February 2024, former Nebraska women's basketball player Ashley Scoggin claimed that the assistant basketball coach at the time, Chuck Love Jr., had manipulated her into a sexual relationship with claims he could "make or break" her playing career. She accused Alberts and the school of not acting on her complaint until she reported it herself to the Title IX office.

Alberts and the university deny the claim and they've asked the judge to dismiss the case.

More troublesome for Alberts was an answer he gave in deposition in December 2025 as reported by FOIAball.com . Scoggin's lawyer Maren Chaloupka asked Alberts about the propriety of a coach having a sexual relationship with a player on the team. Because of the power imbalance, Chaloupka termed such relationships predatory.

Alberts said not all such relationships were predatory, insisting there is "nuance" to the question and said: "It just depends."

"When I was at [University of Nebraska Omaha], we had a worker who was 26-years-old and another student who was in a masters program who is 24," Alberts said, according to a deposition transcript. "Okay. So technically according to you ... this person has power. You respond and report it to Title IX. Is this an issue. It's not an issue because it was a consensual relationship that the two of them have. So that's a different – that's why I'm trying to say there is a little nuance to it."

Chaloupka, pushed back, pointing to a university policy that reads in part: "Faculty members are prohibited from engaging in any romantic relationship with an undergraduate student, regardless of whether the faculty member has any supervisory or evaluative authority over that student."

She also noted that the policy requires faculty to report any such relationships.

While the policy doesn't specfically name coaches and athletes, the school's board of regents has determined that it covers them as well as academic staff, Chaloupka said when questioning Alberts.

In pleadings in the case, Alberts and the university deny mishandling Scoggin's case. Love claims the sex was consensual.

"Is this good cause?" Prescott said. "Because it was out in the public and findable and knowable. His lawyers will say, it's not our fault if you didn't look to your left and look to your right and find what was available to you. And [U-M's] argument will be, it's not our fault if he did these things and we took a minute to find them."

Prescott said both sides erred by not writing a better memorandum of understanding up front. She said the ambiguity likely means both sides have an incentive to settle the case, rather than take it to trial.

"What's the most likely outcome?" Prescott said. "If the University of Michigan pays him some money, because he has some good arguments and that he takes a haircut because wrestling it out of their fingers, it takes time, money, is risky. So the real answer is, they've each given each other a headache here and enough ground to fight and enough ground to settle their differences."

Gordon said Alberts' answer to the deposition question about coaches having sexual relationshiops with athletes looks bad, but it doesn't have to be disqualifying.

"Why is this a deal-breaker?" Gordon said. "It's easily remedied. Why don't they just have this guy, who's their hot pick and they think is the go-to guy, why don't you just have him sign a statement affirming, confirming, agreeing: No coach should have a relationship with a student."

With a final contract still in the works, such language could have been included to clear up any ambiguity, Gordon said.
